chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who drinks wine, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty days.
ai.seo_question: How long are prayers not accepted if one drinks wine?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a specific legal ruling where the consumption of wine results in the non-acceptance of prayers for forty days, reflecting the severity of the sin in Shia jurisprudence. This period aligns with the concept of *ajl* (a fixed term) often cited in hadith literature for expiation or divine punishment, emphasizing the spiritual impurity that temporarily hinders the connection between the worshipper and God.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who drinks the wine, his Prayer would not be Accepted from him for forty days’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajj aj who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one drinks wine his Salat (prayer) is not accepted for forty days.’”
